{{Short description|Norwegian physicist}}
'''Fredrik Christian Grønvold''' (16 June 1924 – 24 October 2015) was a Norwegian chemist.

Born in [[Oslo]], he [[examen artium|finished]] his secondary education at [[Oslo Cathedral School]] in 1943. He studied at the [[University of Oslo]] before receiving a scholarship to take the master of science degree at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1951. He was appointed as an [[associate professor]] at the University of Oslo in 1952, specializing in [[inorganic chemistry]].<ref name=obit1/> He was promoted to [[docent]] in 1959<ref>{{cite news|title=Nye professorer og dosenter|date=13 July 1959|work=Nationen|page=6|language=no}}</ref> and professor in 1985.<ref name=obit1/> He was inducted into the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] in 1988.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26857|title=Norske medlemmer|publisher=Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters|access-date=2 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715142138/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26857|archive-date=15 July 2007}}</ref>

Grønvold was also a board member of the [[Norwegian Industrial Property Office]].<ref name=obit1/> He died at [[Bærum Hospital]] in October 2015, aged 91.<ref name=obit1>{{cite news|title=Fredrik Grønvold|type=obituary|author1=[[Svein Stølen]]|author2=[[Helmer Fjellvåg]]|date=3 November 2015|work=Aftenposten|page=24|language=no}}</ref>
